voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: Singapore, eighteen nineteen. At the river mouth, workers found a great boulder split in two, carved with writing no one could read.
Three metres tall, its halves facing each other. About fifty lines of carved script.
In eighteen forty-three, the acting settlement engineer had it blown up, to widen the river mouth and make room for a fort.
A few pieces were shipped to Calcutta. One came back. It is in Singapore's National Museum.
Scholars have proposed scripts, languages and dates. The inscription has never been fully deciphered.
